title: Efficient Non-Uniform Quantum Hermite Transform through Adaptive Sampling
abstract: On the span of the first $N$ oscillator modes, Gauss--Hermite quadrature gives an exact change of basis between mode coefficients and $N$ weighted position space samples. We implement this transform with $O(N\operatorname{polylog}(N,1/\varepsilon))$ logical gates and polylogarithmic quantum width. The operator-error bound $\varepsilon$ holds on arbitrary superpositions and includes all auxiliary registers. The construction uses signed averages on adaptive windows to convert uniform-grid samples into weighted Hermite-root samples. Their varying widths control the amplification cost, giving the near-linear bound.
summary: This paper develops an efficient quantum circuit for the Quantum Hermite Transform, which maps coefficients in the Hermite basis to weighted position samples. By utilizing adaptive sampling techniques, the authors achieve a near-linear gate complexity, making it a powerful tool for simulating quantum harmonic oscillator dynamics and related quantum processes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the development of an efficient quantum circuit for performing the change of basis between mode coefficients (Hermite basis) and weighted position space samples, known as the Quantum Hermite Transform.
main_result: They achieve a near-linear gate complexity, $O(N 	ext{ polylog}(N, 1/\epsilon))$, for implementing this transform using Clifford+T quantum circuits.
method: The core method involves converting uniform-grid samples to non-uniform, weighted Hermite-root samples using signed averages on adaptive windows, which is realized via complex quantum circuit constructions.
model_or_system: The system is based on the first $N$ oscillator modes, spanned by normalized Hermite functions, relating coefficients to weighted samples at the roots of the $N$-th Hermite polynomial.
key_observables: Transform matrix elements, operator error bound $\epsilon$, mode populations $p_k(\Delta t)$, and off-diagonal coherence terms $\langle k|ho_{out}|\ellangle$.
important_parameters: The number of modes $N$, the error tolerance $\epsilon$, and the time evolution parameter $t$ for QHO dynamics.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the transform is applied to arbitrary superpositions and includes all auxiliary registers, though some results are limited to retained Hermite modes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 demonstrates the transform applied to coherent state evolution (QHO) and even cat state rotation (FrFT). Figure S2 shows simulated mode populations for $N=16$ under specific qubit relaxation parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for the transform, detailing the mathematical conversion from uniform to weighted roots, deriving the required operator $R$, and finally constructing the full quantum circuit realization and analyzing noise diagnostics via the transform–idle–inverse protocol.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, resource-bounded quantum algorithm for a fundamental transform (Hermite basis change) crucial for simulating quantum harmonic oscillators and related quantum field theories, directly impacting quantum simulation protocols.
